I've had first hand pleasure of dealing with maintaining codebases originally written by outsourced Indian devs who stored all dates as "04/20/2015" (Strings) in the database, expecting US format. Then I had to change it over for Europeans. Suddenly some of the original posts were showing up at January 1, 1970. WTF happened? ... oh, just blatant stupidity.

For those who maybe don't initially get it - you can't just convert that to European format - because suddenly that day above becomes "The 04th day of the 20th month of the year 2015" which obviously makes no sense. The more complicated issue was that some of the more recent posts before that issue was discovered had been made expecting the site was already European-date-format friendly. So when I looked at the database and saw "04/05/2015" two times - one of them might have actually been made in America so April 5th, 2015, and the other may have been made in Europe and expected that it was May 04th, 2015. Since these dates corresponded to newsletter links I was able to follow the links through and verify the original publication date and fix them appropriately, and of course any ones that wouldn't make sense when switched were obvious which format they should have been so I handled those cases quickly then moved on to the corner cases. But by changing to using Timestamps measuring seconds since Epoch you can easily convert that integer value into any date/time format system you want.
Help save scientists some sanity. If you submit and or collect timestamped data please use the Unix Epoch or ISO 8601.
